policy: Only authoritative URLs actually opened are recorded. Dynamic counts carry an explicit edition or access date; unresolved printed claims remain unscored.

groups.topic: ISFR 2023 national forest and tree cover
findings: ISFR 2023 reports forest and tree cover of 827,356.95 km² (25.17%), forest cover of 715,342.61 km² (21.76%), and tree cover of 112,014.34 km² (3.41%).
The report confirms that FSI has published nationwide biennial forest-resource assessments since 1987 and that ISFR 2023 is the eighteenth assessment.
All scored questions must distinguish Forest Cover from Tree Cover and retain the ISFR 2023 edition label.

groups.topic: Mangrove cover and Andhra Pradesh district table
findings: ISFR 2023 gives national mangrove cover as 4,991.68 km², a decline of 7.43 km² from the revised 2021 raster assessment.
The official Odisha row is 259.06 km² in 2023 with a +1.55 km² change; the book's visually printed row is internally inconsistent and must be shown as a labelled print error.
Andhra Pradesh rises from 408.42 km² to 421.43 km² (+13.01 km²).
The official AP district table includes Eluru at 0.02 km² and lists SPSR Nellore only once; the book duplicates Nellore and should be corrected transparently.

Official 2023 AP district totals include Krishna 148.45, Kakinada 113.79, Konaseema 74.42, Bapatla 72.92, SPSR Nellore 8.66, Tirupati 1.29, Srikakulam 0.82, Prakasam 0.75, Visakhapatnam 0.31 and Eluru 0.02 km².
NTCA lists 58 tiger reserves across 18 states; any scored total is dated to the current NTCA list.
Madhya Pradesh has nine listed reserves, including Veerangana Durgavati, Ratapani and Madhav; the printed table omits or misclassifies some current entries.
Karnataka's five are Bandipur, Bhadra, Biligiri Ranganatha, Kali and Nagarhole; Kudremukh is not a tiger reserve.
Andhra Pradesh has one tiger reserve, Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam; Telangana has Amrabad and Kawal.
The printed state table will be preserved as a book-edition table, followed by a corrected current NTCA table.
FAO identifies FRA 2025 as its authoritative worldwide assessment based on official national data.
The global chapter must date all country rankings and regional shares to FRA 2025 rather than presenting them as timeless facts.
FAO's technical page confirms a transparent, traceable process using officially nominated national correspondents.

groups.topic: Protected areas and UNESCO biosphere network
findings: WII's current MEE page reports 106 national parks and 574 wildlife sanctuaries; protected-area counts are dynamic and need an access date.
UNESCO designated Cold Desert in September 2025, bringing India to 13 sites in the World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
Cold Desert covers 7,770 km² in Himachal Pradesh and includes Pin Valley National Park and surrounding high-altitude conservation areas.
The national list of 18 Indian biosphere reserves and the UNESCO network list are different datasets and must never be conflated.
